name: The Henderson household at 1816 Prairie Avenue
head: pa1904_henderson_mrs_charles_m

present_on_scene_date.note: Listed at 1816 Prairie Avenue in the Blue Book for 1904 (canvass begun September 1903) and again in the 1905 edition (canvass begun September 1904), which bracket 1 July 1904. The 1905 list prints: 1816 Mrs. Charles M. Henderson.

associated_with.note: The Blue Book's Prairie Avenue street list prints the household at 1816, and the 1905 list again. The book gives no date the household came or went, so neither end is dated here.

not_in_this_household.note: WHO IS NOT ON THIS CARD, AND WHY. The Blue Book is a society register: it names the family members who received and were received, prints unmarried daughters only as '& dr.', and names no young children, servants, coachmen, cooks or nurses. The 1900 census (ED 40, T623 roll 245) was read for this card. The one live-in servant it lists at the house on 1 June 1900 is on the card, graded inferred because the count was taken four years before the scene. Left off: C. M. Henderson (enumerated at Highland Park, where the family was on the census day). The 1910 census was not read. A person goes on this card when a source names them, and not before.

persons.name: Arthur George Parker

born.note: The census gives August 1870, age 29 on 1 June 1900.

occupation.note: Written as "Coachman" in the occupation column on 1 June 1900.

persons.note: Enumerated on 1 June 1900 in the rear building behind the house, as the head of his own household there (coachman); born August 1870 (the figures are hard to read), in England, married. Servants changed places often, so this records who worked here in 1900; no source read says whether this person was still here on 1 July 1904.
